clue.text: Possibly drove around address I shunned

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around or about

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so the I is left out of the word

parts.note: a title is a form of address, such as Sir or Madam

explanation.surface: Someone drove around but avoided calling at a particular address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is a noun: a herd being driven. 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd of animals moved together, and cattle are the classic livestock so driven to market.

clue.text: Source of drink inappropriate in church? Drink's overturned

indicators.note: in places the word for inappropriate inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
off means unsuitable, as in 'that remark was off'

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the drink word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drinks vessel belongs in church, as a drink gets knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for brewing and serving coffee is a vessel from which a drink is poured.

clue.text: Pitfall about motorway for a long walk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pitfall word goes round the motorway letter

parts.note: a pitfall is a trap
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A warning about hazards near a motorway for hikers on a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring journey on foot, as in a tramp across the moors.

clue.text: Language in case where stormy weather penetrates shelter

indicators.note: penetrates means goes inside, so the stormy word sits inside the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
gales are very strong winds, stormy weather

explanation.surface: A description of storms invading a refuge, framed as describing some language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' here is a legal case, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the dense jargon of lawyers, the wording found in documents for a court case.

clue.text: Game — variety of grouse? Lovely

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

indicators.note: a variety of grouse suggests a different version, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shooting party admires a lovely variety of grouse, the game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like game birds, fitting the grouse, but it is the board game Go.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgeous and lovely are synonyms, both meaning beautiful or very attractive.

clue.text: Each seduction punished? It's not very likely

indicators.note: punished means beaten about, so the letters of the two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether every seduction gets punished, and concludes it seldom does.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim possibility, something with little chance of happening, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Big eater to understand about an opening for nutrition

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for understand wraps the other letters

parts.note: to get something is to understand it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to understand something about nutrition, aimed at someone who eats a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gannet is a seabird famed for gulping fish, and in British slang a greedy person.

clue.text: Government official, male, with friends in Arab state

indicators.note: in places the male letter and the friends word inside the Arab country

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula
buds is informal for friends or buddies

explanation.surface: A male government official arrives with his friends in a Gulf country.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints against public bodies.

clue.text: Material challenged in court — end of case

parts.note: to be sued is to be taken to court by a claimant

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word case

explanation.surface: Evidence was challenged in court, bringing the case to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, a fabric used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Father apprehended, but criminal initially escaping, tense

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: escaping means getting away, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to be apprehended is to be caught

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of criminal

explanation.surface: A priest arrested someone, but the crook got away, leaving everyone on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraught atmosphere is anxious and strained, full of nervous tension.

clue.text: Withdraw surprise answer in group

parts.note: to take aback is to surprise or startle

indicators.note: in places the answer letter inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a surprising answer given in a group discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a back seat means stepping back from an active role and letting others lead.

clue.text: Set to secure arrest? That's credible

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the television word encloses the arrest word

parts.note: a telly or tele is a television set
to nab is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: A setup designed to secure an arrest, judged believable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position or theory can be defended and held, so is believable.

clue.text: Put out and cross, blocking recording by the Spanish

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing from within, so the cross sits inside the recording

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
X is a cross shape
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed and frustrated by a Spanish recording being blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' and 'cross' both look like annoyance, but cross is just the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to eject or force out, as from a school or a party.

clue.text: Writer's material recalled stuff for one reflecting critical situation

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the writing material is read backwards

parts.note: ink is what a writer uses
to stuff is to feed, cram with food

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the example abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A writer's work, called back after reflection, puts them in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a knife-edge means a tense, finely balanced moment where things could go either way.

clue.text: Her figure can be so wrong?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a body shape wide at the hips and narrower above, like the fruit
second meaning: in British slang, to go this way is to go badly wrong

explanation.walkthrough: The question frames a body shape as a fault; British slang 'gone pear-shaped' means gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both a body narrow at the top and broad at the base, and plans that have failed.

clue.text: Mechanic, if boarding lorry, starts to examine radiator

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the if goes inside the lorry word

parts.note: an artic is a British articulated lorry, a large truck with a hinged trailer

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A mechanic climbs into a truck to start inspecting its radiator.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, notably a military technician who maintains machinery.

clue.text: Consequence of cold snap seeing setback for this leader of warm place?

indicators.note: a setback is a move backwards, so the frost word is read in reverse

parts.note: rime is frost formed on surfaces, a result of a cold spell

explanation.surface: A ruler of a hot country suffers when an unexpected frost strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the leader is defined by example: a ruler in the hot Gulf states.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler, typically of a hot Middle Eastern state such as Qatar or Kuwait.

clue.text: Curious disposition around City is on the level?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the curious word wraps the City letters

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a bent is a natural inclination or disposition

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an odd temperament in the financial district is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the level' suggests honesty, but here it is literal: lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means lying down, horizontal, as on level ground.

clue.text: Shame when mining rocks, bagging nothing before closure of quarry

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the rearranged letters hold the nothing letter
rocks means shakes up, so the letters of mining are jumbled

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: closure means the end, so the last letter of quarry

explanation.surface: A mining disaster in a quarry brings disgrace, leaving the miners with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' turns MINING into IGNMIN; 'bagging' puts O inside to give IGNOMIN, then the last letter of quarry follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public disgrace or humiliation, a synonym of shame.

clue.text: Carry fifth child?

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A parent wonders about carrying their fifth baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to lug or haul something around, as in toting a bag.

clue.text: Teaching op, with surgery, describing disease

indicators.note: surgery cuts things open and rearranges them, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A teaching operation in a hospital, involving surgery to treat a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'op' looks like the surgery itself, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathogenic is an adjective for agents that cause illness, such as bacteria or viruses.

clue.text: Moral imperative to include name of racial group

indicators.note: to include means to contain, so the moral word holds the name letter

parts.note: an ethic is a moral principle

explanation.surface: A call for moral principles to include the name of every racial group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic relates to a population sharing common descent, culture or nationality.

clue.text: Web image needing time to understand for the present?

parts.note: a GIF is an image format on the internet
ken is knowledge or understanding, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: An internet picture that takes time to make sense of, at least for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present' reads as 'for now', but it means a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift token is a voucher given as a present, exchanged for goods in a shop.

clue.text: Government's foremost official suppressing one lot of trouble

indicators.note: foremost means the very first letter of the government word
suppressing means holding down, so the official covers the one

parts.note: ref is short for referee, the match official
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The government's top official keeps one lot of problems quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief here means hassle or annoyance, as in giving someone grief.

clue.text: Hate having reactive metal when short of sulphur

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the sulphur letter is removed

parts.note: sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone detests handling a volatile metal once the sulphur has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust felt towards someone.

clue.text: Island area accommodating casual business — holiday spot?

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the island and area letters surround the business word

parts.note: biz is informal for business

explanation.surface: An island district hosting relaxed trade, perhaps a vacation destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a destination for sun and nightlife.

clue.text: Anger included feeling when deprived of leader

parts.note: inc is short for included or inclusive

indicators.note: deprived of leader means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a sense is a feeling, as in a sense of dread

explanation.surface: Fury was felt, along with emotion that had lost its direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to enrage, make someone very angry; used here as a verb.

clue.text: Building's effect initially provided in cubes

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of effect
in places the provided word inside the cubes

parts.note: dice are small cubes
if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: The effect of a building made from cubes, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Building's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building or structure.

clue.text: Monarch in backing of business district displays savage attitude

indicators.note: in places the monarch inside the reversed of
backing means moving backwards, so the word of is turned round

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: The monarch backing a financial district shows a savage outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocity is fierce, savage or violent behaviour or temperament.

clue.text: Bad leader not overthrown in middle of battle

indicators.note: in places the reversed not word inside the battle's centre
middle of picks the central pair of letters of battle
overthrown means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nary means not one, as in nary a word

explanation.surface: A poor commander not toppled in the thick of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like a plain negative, but it stands for the dialect word nary, meaning not one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, the archetypal bad leader.
